note: The paper's central theoretical contribution: a componential feedback loop centered on attention shifts instigated by inadequate attentional engagement (IAE), defined as the discrepancy between actual and subjectively desired levels of attentional engagement (FAITHFUL-Tam et al., ~p.251-256).

Adopted as the paper's organizing distinction: 'This review focuses on boredom as a transient affective state,' with trait boredom (boredom proneness) reserved for separate treatment (FAITHFUL-Tam et al., p.251).
Independently theorized in 'Implications for Chronic Boredom'; bifurcated into trait-like attentional weakness vs. malleable non-trait 'long-term factors' (FAITHFUL-Tam et al., p.264-265).

Named as one of three attention-shift routes ('turn inward, e.g., mind-wandering, self-reflection'); independently linked to boredom proneness (positive) and flow proneness (negative) (FAITHFUL-Tam et al., p.256, 264).
Conceptual core of BFM: IAE operationalized via dorsal attention network (DAN) vs. default mode network (DMN) activity, or via dual-task performance cost (FAITHFUL-Tam et al., p.256).

BFM positioned as consistent with and complementary to functional accounts; boredom 'serves a vital function of prompting individuals to direct their attention to... something that is of value' (FAITHFUL-Tam et al., p.263).

'Humans desire to be optimally engaged' is the paper's foundational premise; flow proneness appears as a negative boredom-proneness correlate (FAITHFUL-Tam et al., p.256, citing Harris 2000 at p.264).

Both treated as cognitive-appraisal antecedents of IAE, each independently lowering 'intention to attend' (repetition/O'Hanlon 1981, Daschmann et al. 2011; meaninglessness/Fahlman et al. 2009, Van Tilburg & Igou) (FAITHFUL-Tam et al., p.258-259).
Listed among boredom's characteristic experiential features ('time passing slowly,' citing London & Monello 1974, Martin et al. 2006); not developed into an independent mechanism (FE).

Multidimensional State Boredom Scale (Fahlman et al., 2013); Boredom Proneness Scale (Farmer & Sundberg, 1986); pre/post-block self-report ratings (Hunter & Eastwood, 2016) (FAITHFUL-Tam et al., p.255-256).

Dual-task inference (RT slowing, error-rate increase) as behavioral index of attentional engagement; SART attentional errors correlated with self-reported boredom (Hunter & Eastwood, 2016) (FAITHFUL-Tam et al., p.256, 261).

Rising heart rate and falling skin conductance reported as psychophysiological correlates of boredom, inverse of the engaged-attention profile (Merrifield & Danckert, 2014) (FAITHFUL-Tam et al., p.255-256).

Danckert & Merrifield's (2018) four-condition fMRI study: anticorrelated DMN/anterior-insula activity common to boredom and sustained-attention conditions, distinct from the interest-mood condition; not an EEG-specific measure named anywhere in this source (FAITHFUL-Tam et al., p.255-257).

target: Eastwood, John D., Frischen, A., Fenske, M.J., & Smilek, D. (2012) -- The Unengaged Mind
note: Foundational premise BFM builds on directly: boredom as 'aversive state of wanting but being unable to engage in satisfying activity' (Eastwood et al., 2012, p.484, quoted at ~p.252) (FAITHFUL-Tam et al.).

target: Eastwood, John D., & Gorelik, D. (2019) -- Unused Cognitive Potential (UCP) model
note: BFM extends UCP's 'desire bind'/'unoccupied mind' framing and its bridge between attentional and functional theories into a full process/feedback-loop account (FAITHFUL-Tam et al., p.253, 256).

target: Westgate, Erin C., & Wilson, Timothy D. (2018) -- Meaning and Attentional Components (MAC) model
note: Contests MAC's claim that attention and meaning are orthogonal predictors permitting 'meaningless boredom' under full engagement; BFM argues meaning is a precursor to IAE, not an independent axis, and questions MAC's operationalization of 'attention' as mind-wandering tendency rather than task-related sustained attention (FAITHFUL-Tam et al., p.263-264).

target: Bench, Shane W., & Lench, Heather C. (2013)
note: Boredom as both signal and driving force for pursuit of alternative goals; functional account BFM aligns with (FE).

target: Elpidorou, Andreas (2014) -- The Bright Side of Boredom
note: Cited alongside Elpidorou (2018a) as consistent theorizing on boredom's motivating, regulatory function (FE).

target: Elpidorou, Andreas (2018a) -- The Bored Mind Is a Guiding Mind: Toward a Regulatory Theory of Boredom
note: BFM explicitly positions itself as consistent with Elpidorou's (2018a) regulatory meta-model; 'this places boredom in the role of potentially facilitating personal growth' (FAITHFUL-Tam et al., p.253-254). Same-cluster unit bor-sec-25 (Strand C); direct citation match, not a speculative link.

target: Elpidorou, Andreas (2018b) -- The Good of Boredom
note: Cited as consistent with BFM's chronic-boredom account: 'boredom proneness may be a dysfunction of state boredom' (FAITHFUL-Tam et al., p.264). Same-cluster unit bor-sec-26 (Strand C); direct citation match, not a speculative link.

target: Pekrun, Reinhard (2006) -- Control-Value Theory of Achievement Emotions
note: BFM is 'in line with' control-value theory's value/control appraisal account of academic boredom and 'further incorporates appraisal into the attentional mechanism' (FAITHFUL-Tam et al., p.266).

target: Smith, Craig A., & Ellsworth, Phoebe C. (1985)
note: Earliest cognitive-appraisal profile of boredom: comparatively low perceived control/responsibility, low uncertainty, low effort, low attention relative to other emotions (FAITHFUL-Tam et al., p.254-255).
Three-cause taxonomy of workplace boredom (external, internal, interaction of both); BFM's five-factor antecedent model extends this taxonomy (FAITHFUL-Tam et al., p.257).

target: Leary, Mark R., Rogers, P.A., & Canfield, R.W. (1986)
note: Early attentional account: boredom as 'affective consequence of effortful maintenance of attention to a particular stimulus event' (p.968, quoted at ~p.252) (FAITHFUL-Tam et al.).
fMRI study establishing anticorrelated DMN/anterior-insula activity as a shared signature of boredom-induction and sustained-attention conditions (FAITHFUL-Tam et al., p.255-257).

SART study linking attentional errors to self-reported boredom before/after each task block, cited twice as convergent evidence for IAE and for the feedback loop's dynamic nature (FAITHFUL-Tam et al., p.255-256, 261).
Psychophysiological correlates of boredom: rising heart rate, decreasing skin conductance over time (FAITHFUL-Tam et al., p.255-256).
Originators of the boredom proneness construct/scale, the construct BFM's chronic-boredom account elaborates (FAITHFUL-Tam et al., p.256, 264).

target: Baumeister, Roy F., & Vohs, Kathleen D. (2016) -- strength model of self-regulation
note: One of three self-control mechanisms BFM integrates: effortful attention-redirection depletes limited self-regulatory resources (FAITHFUL-Tam et al., p.262-263).

target: Inzlicht, Michael, & Schmeichel, Brandon J. (2012) -- process model of self-control
note: Second integrated mechanism: the feedback loop shifts priorities from 'have-to' to 'want-to' goals, affecting attention/emotion/motivation (FAITHFUL-Tam et al., p.262-263).

target: Fujita, Kentaro (2008) -- construal-level account of self-control
note: Third integrated mechanism: low-level (vs. high-level) construals of a task increase both boredom and self-control failure (FAITHFUL-Tam et al., p.262-263).
Proposes boredom may confound ego-depletion research by imposing an unwanted self-control demand; BFM engages this emerging discourse directly (FAITHFUL-Tam et al., p.260-261).

target: Milyavskaya, Marina, Inzlicht, M., Hope, N., & Koestner, R. (2019)
note: Boredom-ego-depletion confound speculation; heightened reward sensitivity under boredom cited as consistent with the process-model mechanism (FAITHFUL-Tam et al., p.260, 263).

target: Struk, Andriy A., Carriere, J.S.A., Cheyne, J.A., & Danckert, J. (2017, 2020)
note: Empty-room vs. affordance-rich-room boredom study supporting the desired-engagement-level mechanism (2020); boredom-proneness/mind-wandering association (2017) (FAITHFUL-Tam et al., p.256-257, 264).

target: attention-meaning orthogonality debate (BFM vs. MAC model)
note: Reframes the attention/meaning debate around whether meaning is an independent predictor (MAC) or a precursor to IAE (BFM), proposing these as competing, empirically testable hypotheses (FAITHFUL-Tam et al., p.264).

Resolves the mixed literature on boredom's arousal profile by making arousal direction contingent on where post-IAE attention is directed, rather than a fixed property of boredom (FAITHFUL-Tam et al., p.263-264).

Proposes ego-depletion effects may in some cases reduce to failure to attain adequate attentional engagement rather than prior self-control effort, reframing the confound question (FAITHFUL-Tam et al., p.263).

target: Westgate, Erin C., & Wilson, Timothy D. (2018) Study 1 meta-analysis
note: Notes that MAC's 'attention' operationalization (tendency to focus on one's thoughts) is closer to mind-wandering than to typical task-related sustained-attention measures used elsewhere in boredom research, limiting the conclusiveness of MAC's orthogonality claim (FAITHFUL-Tam et al., p.264).

target: Westgate, Erin C., & Wilson, Timothy D. (2018) Study 2 experimental finding
note: Concedes that Study 2's meaning manipulation had significant effects on both meaning and attentional difficulties -- a finding BFM reads as consistent with meaning being a precursor to attentional difficulties rather than fully orthogonal to attention (FAITHFUL-Tam et al., p.264).

note: ****** UNVERIFIED: BFM's behavioral operationalizations (dual-task RT/error cost; DAN/DMN network balance) plausibly overlap with attention-based measures a VR attention study would collect, but this source uses no pupillometry, gaze/eye-tracking, or EEG; any grounds-measure linkage to the dataset's actual instrumentation requires independent confirmation (P/anticipatory-application).

target: Part III attention/engagement self-report instrument design
note: P/anticipatory-application -- BFM's discrepancy-based IAE construct cautions that identical low-engagement self-report scores could reflect qualitatively different desired-engagement baselines; Part III should consider whether desired-engagement level was ever assessed as a moderator rather than assuming raw engagement scores map directly onto boredom.

target: Part III individual-differences / strata interpretation (desktop-3D vs. video-only; lab-VR vs. deployment-2D-PC)
note: P/anticipatory-application -- BFM's trait-attentional vs. malleable long-term-factor bifurcation of chronic boredom offers two distinct readings of elevated boredom in the deployment/2D-PC pole (stable individual disposition vs. context-specific absence of a desired engagement target), with different intervention implications for design vs. individual-level remediation.

P/anticipatory-application -- BFM's operant/classical-conditioning account of boredom amplification predicts that early inadequate engagement, if uncorrected across a longer or multi-session VLE exposure, should compound rather than plateau, a testable prediction for any Part III data on session length vs. reported boredom/disengagement.
